At this time, when some merchants were crossing the great river of Persia, which is called the Gihon (Oxus),
there was a certain poor man with them, dressed in the garments of beggars (faqīrs).
This man said to the boatmen:
"I am Sultan Jalāl al-Dīn Khwārazmshāh, about whom they say that the Kurds killed me in the mountains of Amid.
For it was not I, but rather my armor-bearer, who was killed;
and behold, for so many years I have been wandering secretly in the world, comforting myself."
The boatmen, however, being afraid,
seized him and brought him to the chiefs of the Mongols who were nearby.
And they tortured him bitterly,
yet he did not deny it until he died,
but rather kept saying, "It is I."
And in the year 1565 [1254 AD],
‘Izz al-Dīn of Iconium,
that he should go in person to serve the Great Khan,
or else armies would enter and lay waste to his country.
And when he was pressured both from within and from without to go,
he reluctantly reached Sebastia, while indulging in riotous living and various kinds of shameful deeds.
For wherever he heard of a woman or a daughter or a son of any of the grandees or the common people,
he would take them by force and ruin them.
And on account of this, the grandees hated him,
and they wanted to make his middle brother, who is Rukn al-Dīn, king in his place.
And when he heard this, he was afraid,
and returned again to Iconium,
and prepared his youngest brother, who is ‘Alā’ al-Dīn, and sent him to do homage to the Khan.
And he wrote a letter with him:
"Behold, I have sent my younger brother, who is ‘Alā’ al-Dīn, who was sultan along with me.
And as for me, because Jalāl al-Dīn Qarāṭāy, my atabeg, died,
and an enemy has risen up against me from the west,
I was not able to come;
surely, at another time I will come."
And when that young brother and the grandees who were with him departed,
he died on the way through the treachery of the grandees themselves.
And ‘Izz al-Dīn and Rukn al-Dīn remained in Iconium.
And when ‘Izz al-Dīn heard of the death of his young brother,
he wanted to seize and destroy the middle brother as well,
so that he might remain alone.
And when the grandees perceived this,
they helped Rukn al-Dīn escape.
